answer: An island fire-monitoring market should avoid making new accounts a haven for free votes. Each agent bidding to locate an ember must burn tokens for voting credits: one destroyed token buys one credit, with no signup allocation. Validators verify the burn on the ledger and mark its output consumed before issuing credits. Splitting credits among aliases leaves total weight unchanged; self-trading cannot restore burned tokens. An attacker seeking n times the voting weight must destroy n times the value, so names alone confer no power.
